title.en: Volume 283 Biographies 70: Jue Luo Wu Mo Ne, Shu Lan, Tu Li Chen, He Guozong
title.raw: 卷283 列傳七十 觉罗武默讷 舒兰 图理琛 何国宗

sentences.zh: 列傳七十

translations.literal: Biographies 70
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 70

sentences.zh: 覺羅武默訥舒蘭拉錫拉錫子旺札爾孫博靈阿圖理琛何國宗

translations.literal: Jue Luo Wumune, Shulan, Laxi, Laxi's son Wangzhar, Sun Boling'a, Tulichen, and He Guozong
translations.idiomatic: Jue Luo Wumune, Shulan, Laxi, Wangzhar son of Laxi, Sun Boling'a, Tulichen, and He Guozong

sentences.zh: 覺羅武默訥，正黃旗人，景祖第三兄索長阿四世孫也。

translations.literal: Jue Luo Wumune was a man of the Plain Yellow Banner, a fourth-generation descendant of Suochang'a, the third elder brother of Emperor Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Wumune of the Jue Luo clan, a Plain Yellow Bannerman, was a fourth-generation descendant of Suochang'a, the third elder brother of the dynastic founder Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 順治四年，授世職拖沙喇哈番，累進三等阿達哈哈番，擢一等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi he was granted the hereditary rank of tuosashala hafan, was promoted step by step to third-rank adaha hafan, and was raised to first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 4 (1647) he received the hereditary office of tuosashala hafan, rose through successive promotions to third-rank adaha hafan, and was appointed a first-class imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，授內大臣，管佐領。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was appointed Grand Minister of the Interior and placed in charge of a company.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 (1667) he was made a Grand Minister of the Interior and given charge of a banner company.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命偕侍衛費耀色、塞護禮、索鼐瞻禮長白山，諭曰：「長白山祖宗發祥之地，爾等赴吉林，選識路之人，瞻視行禮，並巡視寧古塔諸處，於大暑前馳驛速往。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered, together with the bodyguards Fei Yaose, Sai Huli, and Suonai, to pay reverence at Changbai Mountain. He was instructed: 'Changbai Mountain is the place where our forefathers arose. You are to go to Jilin, choose men who know the route, behold the mountain and perform the rites, and also inspect the region around Ningguta. Travel post-haste and arrive before the Great Heat.'
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 (1677) he was sent with the guardsmen Fei Yaose, Sai Huli, and Suonai to worship at Changbai Mountain. The emperor told them: 'Changbai Mountain is where our imperial ancestors first rose. Go to Jilin, find guides who know the way, perform the rites of veneration, and inspect the districts around Ningguta. Ride the courier routes and reach there before the height of summer.'

sentences.zh: 」五月己卯，武默訥等發京師；

translations.literal: ' On the day jimao in the fifth month, Wumune and the others set out from the capital;
translations.idiomatic: ' On jimao day in the fifth month, Wumune and his party left the capital;

sentences.zh: 己丑，至盛京，東行；

translations.literal: on the day jichou they reached Shengjing and traveled east;
translations.idiomatic: on jichou day they reached Mukden and continued east;

sentences.zh: 戊戌，至吉林。

translations.literal: on the day wuxu they reached Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: on wuxu day they arrived at Jilin.

sentences.zh: 詢土人，無知長白山路者。

translations.literal: They questioned the local people, but none knew the route to Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: They asked the locals, yet none knew the road to Changbai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 得舊居額赫訥殷獵戶岱穆布魯，言其父曾獵長白山麓，負鹿歸，道經三宿，似去額赫訥殷不遠。

translations.literal: They found a hunter named Daimuburu who had formerly lived at Ehene Yin. He said his father had once hunted at the foot of Changbai Mountain, carried a deer back, and spent three nights on the road, which seemed not far from Ehene Yin.
translations.idiomatic: They found Daimuburu, a hunter who had once lived at Ehene Yin. He said his father had hunted on the lower slopes of Changbai Mountain, brought a deer home on his back, and been three nights on the trail—apparently not far from Ehene Yin.

sentences.zh: 自吉林至額赫訥殷，陸行十日，舟行幾倍之。

translations.literal: From Jilin to Ehene Yin was ten days by land, and nearly several times that by boat.
translations.idiomatic: From Jilin to Ehene Yin was ten days overland; by river the journey took nearly twice as long.

sentences.zh: 寧古塔將軍巴海令運米十七艘詣額赫訥殷，先發，並令協領薩布素護武默訥等行。

translations.literal: Bahai, the general at Ningguta, ordered seventeen grain boats sent to Ehene Yin in advance, and also ordered the assistant commandant Sabusu to escort Wumune and the others on their journey.
translations.idiomatic: Bahai, military governor of Ningguta, sent seventeen grain boats ahead to Ehene Yin and ordered Assistant Commandant Sabusu to escort Wumune's party.

sentences.zh: 六月丁未，武默訥等攜三月糧，陸行經溫德亨河、庫埒訥嶺、奇爾薩河、布爾堪河、納丹弗埒城、輝發江、法河、卓隆鄂河，抵訥殷江乾，米亦至。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei in the sixth month, Wumune and the others carried three months' provisions and traveled overland by way of the Wendehun River, Kule'ne Ridge, the Qiersa River, the Bu'erkan River, Nadanfuluo City, the Huifa River, the Fa River, and the Zhuolong'e River, reaching the headwaters of the Ne Yin River, where the grain also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the sixth month they set out with three months' rations, marching overland past the Wendehun River, Kule'ne Ridge, the Qiersa, Bu'erkan, and Zhuolong'e rivers, Nadanfuluo, the Huifa and Fa rivers, until they reached the upper Ne Yin, where the grain convoy joined them.

sentences.zh: 乃乘小舟，與薩布素分道行，溯訥殷江逆流上。

translations.literal: They then boarded small boats, separated from Sabusu, and went upstream against the current of the Ne Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: They then took small boats, parted from Sabusu's column, and poled upstream on the Ne Yin.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，會於額赫訥殷。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin they met at Ehene Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day they rendezvoused at Ehene Yin.

sentences.zh: 一望深林無路，薩布素率眾前行，伐木開道。

translations.literal: At a glance the deep forest offered no path. Sabusu led the men forward and cut trees to open a way.
translations.idiomatic: Before them lay trackless forest. Sabusu went ahead with his men, felling trees to cut a path.

sentences.zh: 遣人還告：行三十里，得一山，升其巔，緣木而望，長白山乃在百餘里外，片片白光如積玉，視之甚晰。

translations.literal: He sent men back to report: after traveling thirty li they reached a hill; climbing its summit and looking along the treetops, they saw Changbai Mountain more than a hundred li away, patches of white light like piled jade, very clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts returned to say that after thirty li they had climbed a hilltop and, peering over the treetops, sighted Changbai Mountain a hundred-odd li distant—streaks of white like heaped jade, startlingly clear.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，武默訥前行。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Wumune went forward.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Wumune pressed ahead.

sentences.zh: 己巳，遇薩布素於林中。

translations.literal: On the day jisi he met Sabusu in the forest.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he rejoined Sabusu in the woods.

sentences.zh: 壬申黎明，大霧，莫辨山所向。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day renshen there was heavy fog, and they could not tell which way the mountain lay.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on renshen day a thick fog hid the mountain entirely.

sentences.zh: 聞鶴唳，尋聲往，遇鹿蹊，循行至山麓，見周遭密林，中間平迤圓繞，有草無木。

translations.literal: Hearing cranes cry, they went toward the sound, found a deer track, and followed it to the foot of the mountain. They saw dense forest all around, with a level, gently rounded open space in the middle where there was grass but no trees.
translations.idiomatic: They heard cranes calling, followed the sound, picked up a deer trail, and came to the mountain's foot. All around stood thick forest; in the center lay a broad, gently rounded clearing covered in grass but bare of trees.

sentences.zh: 前臨小林，盡處有白樺木，整若栽植，及旋行林外，仍瀰漫無所見。

translations.literal: Before them was a small grove; at its end stood white birches, as neatly arranged as if planted. When they circled outside the grove, fog still enveloped everything and nothing could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead stood a small wood ending in white birches aligned as if planted by hand. They walked around the grove's edge, yet the fog still closed in and hid everything.

sentences.zh: 跪誦敕旨，拜畢，霧開，峰巒歷歷在目，登陟有路。

translations.literal: They knelt, recited the imperial edict, and when the prostration was finished the fog lifted; the peaks stood clearly before them and a path for ascent appeared.
translations.idiomatic: They knelt, read aloud the imperial command, and bowed. When the rite ended the mist parted; the peaks stood sharp before them and a path upward opened.

sentences.zh: 遙望之，山修而扈，既近，則堂平而宇圜，向所睹積玉光，冰雪所凝也。

translations.literal: Seen from afar the mountain was tall and escorted by lesser heights; when they drew near, its main hall was level and its outer precincts round. The piled-jade light they had seen before was ice and snow congealed.
translations.idiomatic: From a distance the mountain rose tall with attendant ridges; up close its summit was broad and its slopes rounded. The jade-like gleam they had glimpsed earlier was compacted ice and snow.

sentences.zh: 山峻約百餘裡，巔有池，環以五峰，其四峰臨水拱峙，正南一峰稍低，分列雙闕。

translations.literal: The mountain rose steep for more than a hundred li. At the summit was a lake encircled by five peaks; four peaks faced the water and arched around it, while the one due south was slightly lower, forming a pair of gate towers.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain climbed steeply for a hundred-odd li. On the summit lay a lake ringed by five peaks: four stood over the water in a guarding arc, while the southern peak, slightly lower, formed a double gateway.

sentences.zh: 池廣袤約三四十里，夾山澗水噴注，自左流者為松花江，右流者為大小訥殷河，繞山皆平林。

translations.literal: The lake was some thirty or forty li in length and breadth. Mountain streams gushed in from both sides; the stream to the left became the Songhua River, that to the right the Greater and Lesser Ne Yin rivers. Around the mountain lay level forest.
translations.idiomatic: The lake stretched thirty or forty li across. Torrents poured in from the ravines on either flank—the left becoming the Songhua, the right the Greater and Lesser Ne Yin. Level woodland circled the mountain below.

sentences.zh: 武默訥瞻拜而下。

translations.literal: Wumune paid reverence and descended.
translations.idiomatic: Wumune worshipped and came down from the summit.

sentences.zh: 峰巔群鹿奔逸，僕其七，墜武默訥等前。

translations.literal: On the summit a herd of deer fled in panic; seven fell prostrate, dropping before Wumune and the others.
translations.idiomatic: A herd of deer bolted across the summit; seven stumbled and fell at Wumune's feet.

sentences.zh: 時登山者正七人，方乏食，謝山靈賜。

translations.literal: Those who had climbed the mountain were exactly seven and were short of food; they thanked the mountain spirit for the gift.
translations.idiomatic: Only seven men had reached the summit and they were nearly out of provisions; they thanked the mountain spirit for the bounty.

sentences.zh: 卻行未里許，欻然霧合。

translations.literal: They had gone back less than a li when the fog suddenly closed in again.
translations.idiomatic: They had retraced their steps less than a li when the mist shut in once more.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，還至前望處，終不復見山光。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou they returned to the place from which they had first looked out, but never again saw the mountain's light.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day they came back to their earlier lookout, yet never again caught sight of the mountain's gleam.

sentences.zh: 七月庚辰，至恰庫河，馬疲甚。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen in the seventh month they reached the Qiaoku River; the horses were utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the seventh month they reached the Qiaoku River, their horses spent.

sentences.zh: 甲申，自恰庫河乘舟還，經色克騰、圖伯赫、噶爾漢、噶達渾、薩穆、薩克錫、法克什、多琿諸河，至松花江。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen they boarded boats at the Qiaoku River to return, passing the Seketeng, Tubohe, Ga'erhan, Gadahun, Samu, Sakexi, Fakeshi, and Duohun rivers, and reaching the Songhua.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day they took boats down from the Qiaoku, threading the Seketeng, Tubohe, Ga'erhan, Gadahun, Samu, Sakexi, Fakeshi, and Duohun rivers until they joined the Songhua.

sentences.zh: 八月丁未，還吉林，巡視寧古塔諸處。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei in the eighth month they returned to Jilin and inspected the districts around Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the eighth month they were back at Jilin and toured the Ningguta region.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，還京師。

translations.literal: On the day yichou they returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，詔封長白山之神，秩祀如五嶽。

translations.literal: When their memorial reached the throne, an edict enfeoffed the spirit of Changbai Mountain, with sacrifices ranked like those to the Five Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Their report reached the throne, and an edict ennobled the spirit of Changbai Mountain with rites equal to those of the Five Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命武默訥齎敕往封，歲時望祭如典禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Wumune was ordered to carry an edict to perform the enfeoffment; seasonal worship from afar followed the established ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 (1678) Wumune was sent with an edict to invest the mountain spirit, and distant seasonal worship thereafter followed court precedent.

sentences.zh: 十九年，召入養心殿，命工繪其像以賜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned to the Hall of Mental Cultivation and ordered that artisans paint his portrait to be bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 (1680) he was received in the Hall of Mental Cultivation and commanded to have his likeness painted and presented to him.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「以此像俾爾子孫世世供享，以昭恩寵。

translations.literal: He was instructed: 'With this portrait let your descendants offer sacrifice generation after generation, to display imperial favor.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: 'Let your descendants worship before this portrait for generations, as a sign of the grace shown you.'

sentences.zh: 」二十九年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: ' In the twenty-ninth year he died and was granted funeral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: ' He died in Kangxi 29 (1690) and was granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 舒蘭，納喇氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Shulan, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shulan of the Nara clan was a Plain Red Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 父敦多哩，官刑部侍郎，兼佐領。

translations.literal: His father Dunduoli served as vice minister of the Ministry of Justice and also held a company command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dunduoli was vice minister of Justice and also commanded a banner company.

sentences.zh: 坐鞫總督蔡毓榮罪，附和尚書希福從輕比，奪官，戍黑龍江。

translations.literal: For trying the case of Governor-General Cai Yurong's crime, he followed Minister Xifu in applying a lenient comparison, was stripped of office, and was banished to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: While investigating Governor-General Cai Yurong's offense he sided with Minister Xifu in urging leniency, lost his post, and was exiled to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 舒蘭自理籓院筆帖式遷主事。

translations.literal: Shulan rose from a clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs to section chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shulan advanced from a clerk in the Court of Colonial Affairs to section chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年，從侍郎滿丕、都統烏達禪等，招降巴爾瑚三千餘人，安置察哈爾游牧地，編隸佐領。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi, together with Vice Minister Manpi, Commander-in-Chief Udazan, and others, he induced more than three thousand Barhu to submit, settled them on Chahar pasturelands, and registered them under banner companies.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 (1699) he joined Vice Minister Manpi and Commander-in-Chief Udazan in receiving the submission of over three thousand Barhu, resettling them on Chahar grazing lands under banner companies.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巴爾瑚佐領額克圖叛，戕察哈爾副總管阿必達、驍騎校班第，掠馬駝以遁。

translations.literal: Before long the Barhu company commander Eketu rebelled, killed the Chahar deputy commander Abida and the brave-rider captain Bandi, and fled after seizing horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the Barhu company officer Eketu rebelled, murdered Chahar Deputy Commander Abida and Captain Bandi, and fled with stolen horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 上命喀爾喀公錫卜推哈坦等率蒙古兵追剿，舒蘭持檄傳示蒙古諸貝勒台吉，並徵察哈爾、厄魯特兵，從烏達禪會剿，擒其渠。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Khalkha duke Sibutuihatan and others to lead Mongol troops in pursuit. Shulan carried proclamations to the Mongol princes and taiji, also mobilized Chahar and Oirat troops, joined Udazan in the joint campaign, and captured the rebel leader.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Khalkha duke Sibutuihatan with Mongol cavalry in pursuit. Shulan bore edicts to the Mongol nobles, mustered Chahar and Oirat auxiliaries, joined Udazan's column, and took the ringleader.

sentences.zh: 遷內閣侍讀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Reader in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Reader in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四十年，命偕侍衛拉錫往探河源，諭曰：「河源雖名古爾班索里瑪勒，其發源處人跡罕到。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was ordered, together with the bodyguard Laxi, to explore the source of the Yellow River. He was instructed: 'Although the river's source is called Gurban Suurimale, its place of origin is rarely reached by human foot.'
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 40 (1701) he was sent with the guardsman Laxi to trace the Yellow River to its source. The emperor said: 'The headwaters are called Gurban Suurimale, yet almost no traveler reaches the place where they rise.'

sentences.zh: 爾等務窮其源，察視河流自何處入雪山邊內。

translations.literal: You must trace it to the utmost source and observe from where the river enters within the snowy mountains' border.
translations.idiomatic: You must follow it to the farthest spring and note where the stream first enters the inner country beyond the snow ranges.

sentences.zh: 凡經流諸處，宜詳閱之。

translations.literal: Every place the river passes should be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Every stretch the river traverses should be surveyed with care.

sentences.zh: 」四月辛酉，舒蘭等發京師。

translations.literal: ' On the day xinyou in the fourth month, Shulan and the others set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: ' On xinyou day in the fourth month Shulan's party left the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月己亥，至青海。

translations.literal: On the day jihai in the fifth month they reached Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the fifth month they reached Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 庚子，至庫庫布拉克。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi they reached Kukubulak.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day they arrived at Kukubulak.

sentences.zh: 貝勒色卜騰扎勒與偕行。

translations.literal: The beile Sebutengzhale traveled with them.
translations.idiomatic: The beile Sebutengzhale accompanied them.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，至鄂棱諾爾。

translations.literal: On the day guihai in the sixth month they reached Eling Nor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the sixth month they reached Lake Eling.

sentences.zh: 甲子，西行至扎棱諾爾。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi they traveled west to Zhaling Nor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day they went west to Lake Zhaling.

sentences.zh: 鄂棱週二百餘裡，扎棱週三百餘裡，二諾爾距三十里許。

translations.literal: Eling measured more than two hundred li in circumference, Zhaling more than three hundred li; the two lakes were about thirty li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Eling was over two hundred li around, Zhaling over three hundred; the two lakes lay some thirty li apart.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，至星宿海，蒙古名「鄂敦塔拉」。

translations.literal: On the day yichou they reached the Sea of Stars, called in Mongol 'Odun Tala.'
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day they reached the Sea of Stars, known in Mongol as Odun Tala.

sentences.zh: 星宿海之源，小泉萬億，歷歷如星，眾山環之。

translations.literal: At the source of the Sea of Stars were myriads of small springs, each distinct like a star, with many mountains encircling them.
translations.idiomatic: At its source countless little springs glittered like stars, ringed by mountains on every side.

sentences.zh: 南有山曰古爾班圖勒哈，西南有山曰布瑚珠勒赫，西有山曰巴爾布哈，北有山曰阿克塔齊勒，東北有山曰烏闌都什，蒙古總名曰「庫爾坤」，即崑崙也。

translations.literal: To the south was a mountain called Gurban Tuleha; to the southwest, Buhuzulehe; to the west, Barbuha; to the north, Aktaqile; to the northeast, Ulandushi. In Mongol they were collectively called 'Kulun,' that is, Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: South stood Gurban Tuleha; southwest, Buhuzulehe; west, Barbuha; north, Aktaqile; northeast, Ulandushi—the Mongol name for the whole range was Kulun, the Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 山泉出自古爾班圖勒哈者，為噶爾瑪瑭；

translations.literal: The spring from Gurban Tuleha was called Garma Tang;
translations.idiomatic: The stream from Gurban Tuleha was the Garma Tang;

sentences.zh: 出自巴爾布哈者，為噶爾瑪楚木朗；

translations.literal: that from Barbuha was Garma Chumulang;
translations.idiomatic: from Barbuha, the Garma Chumulang;

sentences.zh: 出自阿克塔齊勒者，為噶爾瑪沁尼。

translations.literal: and that from Aktaqile was Garma Qinni.
translations.idiomatic: from Aktaqile, the Garma Qinni.

sentences.zh: 三山之泉，溢為三支河，即古爾班索里瑪勒也。

translations.literal: The springs of the three mountains overflowed into three branches, which together were Gurban Suurimale.
translations.idiomatic: These three mountain springs fed three branches that together formed Gurban Suurimale.

sentences.zh: 三河東流入扎棱諾爾，扎棱一支入鄂棱諾爾，黃河自鄂棱出。

translations.literal: The three rivers flowed east into Zhaling Nor; one branch of Zhaling entered Eling Nor, and the Yellow River issued from Eling.
translations.idiomatic: All three ran east into Zhaling; one arm of Zhaling fed Eling, and the Yellow River issued from Eling.

sentences.zh: 其他山泉與平地水泉，淵淪縈繞，不可勝數，悉歸黃河東下。

translations.literal: Other mountain springs and lowland springs wound and pooled in numbers beyond counting, all joining the Yellow River flowing east.
translations.idiomatic: Countless other hill springs and marsh pools spiraled together and all fed the river eastward.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，舒蘭等自星宿海還，舍故道，循河流東南行。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Shulan and the others left the Sea of Stars, abandoned the former route, and followed the river southeast.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day they left the Sea of Stars, forsook their inbound trail, and traced the river southeast.

sentences.zh: 己巳，登哈爾吉山，見黃河折而東，至庫庫陀羅海山，又南繞薩楚克山，复北流，經巴爾陀羅海山之南。

translations.literal: On the day jisi they climbed Ha'erji Mountain and saw the Yellow River bend east; it reached Kukutuoluohai Mountain, then curved south around Sachuke Mountain, turned north again, and passed south of Ba'ertuoluohai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day they climbed Ha'erji Mountain and watched the Yellow River bend east toward Kukutuoluohai, loop south around Sachuke, swing north again, and run along the south flank of Ba'ertuoluohai.

sentences.zh: 庚午，達阿木尼瑪勒佔穆遜山，山最高，雲霧蔽之，不可端倪。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu they reached Amunimale Zhanmuxun Mountain. It was the highest; clouds and mist veiled it so its limits could not be discerned.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day they reached Amunimale Zhanmuxun, the loftiest peak, wrapped in cloud so that its full extent could not be seen.

sentences.zh: 蒙古人言長三百餘裡，有九高峰，積冰終古不消。

translations.literal: Mongols said it was more than three hundred li long, with nine lofty peaks whose piled ice never melted through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Mongols said the range ran three hundred-odd li with nine towering summits whose ice never thawed.

sentences.zh: 常雨雪，一月得晴僅三四日。

translations.literal: Snow and rain were constant; in a month there were only three or four clear days.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and sleet were almost constant; a month might bring only three or four days of clear sky.

sentences.zh: 舒蘭等自此返。

translations.literal: Shulan and the others returned from this point.
translations.idiomatic: From here Shulan and his companions turned back.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至錫喇庫特勒，又南過僧庫爾高嶺，更百餘裡，至黃河岸。

translations.literal: On the day renshen they reached Xilakutile, then went south over Sengku'er Gaoling, and after another hundred-odd li reached the Yellow River bank.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day they reached Xilakutile, crossed Sengku'er Pass to the south, and after another hundred-odd li stood on the Yellow River's bank.

sentences.zh: 見黃河自巴爾陀羅海山東北流，經歸德堡北、達喀山南兩山峽中，流入蘭州。

translations.literal: They saw the Yellow River flow northeast from Ba'ertuoluohai Mountain, pass north of Guide Fort and through the gorge between Daka Mountain to the south and another peak, and enter Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They saw the river run northeast from Ba'ertuoluohai, thread the gorge north of Guide with Daka Mountain to the south, and flow on toward Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自京師至星宿海，七千六百餘裡。

translations.literal: From the capital to the Sea of Stars was more than seven thousand six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The capital lay more than seven thousand six hundred li from the Sea of Stars.

sentences.zh: 寧夏西自松山至星宿海，天氣漸低，地勢漸高，人氣閉塞，行多喘息。

translations.literal: West of Ningxia, from Songshan to the Sea of Stars, the air grew thinner as the ground rose higher; breath was stifled and travelers often gasped.
translations.idiomatic: West of Ningxia, from Songshan up to the Sea of Stars, the air thinned as the land climbed; travelers labored for breath at every step.

sentences.zh: 九月，還京師，具疏述所經，並繪圖以進。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they returned to the capital, submitted a memorial detailing their route, and presented maps.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they were back in the capital with a memorial of their route and maps for the throne.

sentences.zh: 上諭廷臣曰：「朕於古今山川名號，雖在邊徼遐荒，必詳考圖籍，廣詢方言，務得其正。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the court: 'As to the names of mountains and rivers ancient and modern, even in remote borderlands I must examine maps and records in detail, inquire widely into local speech, and secure the correct forms.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: 'Whether a place name is ancient or modern, even in the farthest borderlands I study the maps, question local usage, and insist on the correct form.'

sentences.zh: 故遣使至崑崙，目擊詳求，載入輿圖。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent envoys to Kunlun to investigate on the spot and enter the findings in the imperial atlas.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I sent envoys to Kunlun to see for themselves and record what they found on the imperial maps.

sentences.zh: 即如黃河源出西塞外庫爾坤山之東，眾泉渙散，燦如列星，蒙古謂之'鄂敦塔拉'，西番謂之'索里瑪勒'，中華謂之'星宿海'，是為河源。

translations.literal: Take the Yellow River: its source lies east of Kulun Mountain beyond the western passes. Myriad springs scatter and glitter like stars in array. Mongols call it 'Odun Tala,' Tibetans 'Suurimale,' and Chinese 'the Sea of Stars'—this is the river's source.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River, for example, rises east of Kulun beyond the western frontier. Countless springs spread out like a constellation: Mongols call the place Odun Tala, Tibetans Suurimale, Chinese the Sea of Stars—that is the source.

sentences.zh: 彙為扎棱、鄂棱二澤。

translations.literal: They gather into the two lakes Zhaling and Eling.
translations.idiomatic: The waters pool in the twin lakes Zhaling and Eling.

sentences.zh: 東南行，折北，復東行，由歸德堡、積石關入蘭州，其原委可得而縷晰也。

translations.literal: Flowing southeast, bending north, then east again, it passes Guide Fort and Jishi Pass into Lanzhou; its course can thus be traced strand by strand.
translations.idiomatic: It runs southeast, bends north, then east again through Guide and Jishi Pass into Lanzhou—its entire course can now be traced in detail.

sentences.zh: 舒蘭累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: Shulan was promoted step by step to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Shulan rose through successive promotions to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，命往西藏封拉藏為翊法恭順汗。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was ordered to Tibet to enfeoff Lozang as the Yifa Gongshun Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 45 (1706) he was sent to Tibet to invest Lozang as the Supporting-the-Dharma, Respectful and Obedient Khan.

sentences.zh: 回京得風疾，遣太醫診視。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he suffered a wind ailment, and imperial physicians were sent to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he fell ill with a paralytic disorder, and court physicians were dispatched to attend him.

sentences.zh: 越二年，疾復發，乞休，許解任調治。

translations.literal: After two years the illness recurred; he requested retirement and was permitted to leave office to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the malady returned; he asked to retire and was allowed to leave his post to recover.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，疾愈，起故官。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, when he had recovered, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 52 (1713), cured of his illness, he was recalled to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 是年以萬壽恩典，復其父敦多哩故秩。

translations.literal: That year, by the grace of the Longevity celebration, his father Dunduoli's former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as part of the imperial birthday amnesty, his father Dunduoli's former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事，降三秩調用。

translations.literal: Before long, for an offense, he was demoted three ranks and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was implicated in an offense, stripped of three ranks, and transferred to a lesser post.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 59 (1720).

sentences.zh: 拉錫，圖伯特氏，蒙古正白旗人。

translations.literal: Laxi, of the Tubote clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Laxi of the Tubote clan was a Plain White Banner Mongol.

sentences.zh: 自親軍校三遷二等侍衛，偕舒蘭窮河源，進一等。

translations.literal: From an imperial guards cadet he was promoted three times to second-class bodyguard; together with Shulan he traced the river to its source and was advanced to first class.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from an imperial guards cadet through three promotions to second-class guardsman; after tracing the Yellow River's source with Shulan he was made a first-class guardsman.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，累擢本旗都統。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongzheng reign he was promoted step by step to commander-in-chief of his banner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he rose to commander-in-chief of his banner.

sentences.zh: 以治事明敏，予拜他喇布勒哈番世職，授議政大臣。

translations.literal: For clear and keen administration he was granted the hereditary rank of baitalabule hafan and appointed a Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for sharp and capable administration, he received the hereditary rank of baitalabule hafan and a seat on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 拉錫諳習旗務，奏事輒稱旨，累被褒嘉，加授拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: Laxi was thoroughly versed in banner affairs; his memorials always met with approval, he was repeatedly praised, and was additionally granted tuosashala hafan.
translations.idiomatic: Laxi knew banner administration inside out; his reports consistently pleased the throne, he won repeated commendation, and received an additional grant of tuosashala hafan.

sentences.zh: 四年，以隱匿烏梁海事，盡削官職，降授一等侍衛，管太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for concealing an Ulianghai affair, all his offices were stripped; he was demoted to first-class bodyguard and put in charge of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726) he lost every post for covering up an Ulianghai scandal and was reduced to first-class guardsman while serving as superintendent of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋仍擢鑲白旗滿洲都統，迭署江寧將軍、天津滿洲水師營都統，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon reappointed commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner Manchus, acted successively as Jiangning military governor and head of the Tianjin Manchu naval camp, and became Grand Minister of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was again promoted to commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner Manchus, served in turn as acting military governor of Jiangning and commander of the Tianjin Manchu naval camp, and was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子旺札爾，初授侍衛，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Wangzhar entered service as a guardsman and inherited the family rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wangzhar was first appointed bodyguard and inherited the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 使從侍郎阿克敦與噶爾丹定界。

translations.literal: He accompanied Vice Minister Akedun on the mission to fix the border with Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: On mission he followed Vice Minister Akedun in delimiting the border with Galdan.

sentences.zh: 如蘇州、如浙江按事。

translations.literal: He conducted investigations in Suzhou and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent on investigation to Suzhou and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 累遷鑲白旗滿洲都統、理籓院侍郎、御前大臣。

translations.literal: He rose to Bordered White Banner commander-in-chief, vice minister of Colonial Affairs, and imperial attendant minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to commander-in-chief of the Bordered White Banner Manchus, vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 命赴金川察沿途驛站。

translations.literal: The court sent him to Jinchuan to inspect courier stations along the way.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to go to Jinchuan to inspect the relay stations along the route.

sentences.zh: 金川平，擢領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: After the Jinchuan campaign he was made Grand Minister of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinchuan was pacified he was promoted to Grand Minister of the Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡恪慎。

translations.literal: He died and received the posthumous name Ke-shen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Ke-shen.

sentences.zh: 孫博靈阿，襲世職。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Boling'a succeeded to the hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Boling'a inherited the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛，累遷正藍旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: He began as a guardsman and rose to Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed bodyguard and was promoted step by step to Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 從征金川，攻當噶爾拉，撲碉受創，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jinchuan war he assaulted Dangga'erla, rushed a blockhouse, was wounded, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jinchuan campaign he attacked Dangga'erla, stormed a blockhouse, was wounded, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈都統銜，進世職一等輕車都尉，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given commander-in-chief rank, his hereditary title was raised to first-class commandant of light chariots, and his image was enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the rank of commander-in-chief, advanced in hereditary office to first-class commandant of light chariots, and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十七年，高宗命侍衛阿彌達詣西寧祭河神，再窮河源。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 47 (1782) the Gaozong sent the guardsman Amita to Xining to worship the River God and again seek the river's source.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong the Gaozong ordered the guardsman Amita to go to Xining to sacrifice to the River God and once more trace the Yellow River to its source.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「星宿海西南有水名阿勒坦郭勒，更西有巨石高數丈，名阿勒坦噶達素齊老。

translations.literal: He reported on his return: 'Southwest of the Sea of Stars lies a stream named Altan Gol; farther west stands a rock several zhang high called Altan Kadak Su Qilao.'
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized: 'Southwest of the Sea of Stars is a stream called Altan Gol; farther west is a boulder several zhang high called Altan Kadak Su Qilao.'

sentences.zh: 蒙古語'阿勒坦'為黃金，'噶達素'為北極星，'郭勒'為河，'齊老'石也。

translations.literal: In Mongol altan means gold, kadak su the pole star, gol a river, and qilao a stone.
translations.idiomatic: In Mongol 'altan' means gold, 'kadak su' the pole star, 'gol' a river, and 'qilao' a stone.

sentences.zh: 崖壁黃金色，上有池，池中泉噴湧，釃為百道，皆黃金色。

translations.literal: Golden cliffs rose above a pool whose springs burst out in a hundred golden streams.
translations.idiomatic: The cliff face was golden in color; above was a pool whose springs gushed forth, dividing into a hundred channels, all golden in hue.

sentences.zh: 入阿勒坦郭勒，迴旋三百餘裡，入星宿海，為黃河真源。

translations.literal: These waters entered the Altan Gol, circled more than three hundred li, and joined the Sea of Stars—the river's true source.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the Altan Gol, wound three hundred-odd li, and entered the Sea of Stars—this was the true source of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 」高宗命四庫館諸臣輯河源紀略識其事。

translations.literal: ' The Gaozong had Siku scholars compile an account of the river source to document the finding.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Gaozong ordered scholars of the Siku project to compile a record of the river source to commemorate the event.

sentences.zh: 阿彌達更名阿必達。

translations.literal: Amita was renamed Abida.
translations.idiomatic: Amita was renamed Abida.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂子，附見阿桂傳。

translations.literal: Son of Grand Secretary Agui; see the biography of Agui.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Grand Secretary Agui; see Agui's biography.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛，阿顏覺羅氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Tulichen of the Ayanggioro clan was a Plain Yellow Banner Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen, of the Ayanggioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以國子生考授內閣中書，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: Selected from the Imperial Academy as a Grand Secretariat secretary, he became a Reader.
translations.idiomatic: As a student of the Imperial Academy he passed examination for secretary in the Grand Secretariat and was transferred to Reader.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪職。

translations.literal: He lost his post for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年，特命復職，出使土爾扈特。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 51 (1712) he was specially reinstated and dispatched to the Torghuts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he was specially ordered restored and sent as envoy to the Torghuts.

sentences.zh: 初，土爾扈特汗阿玉奇從子阿喇布珠爾，假道準噶爾赴西藏謁達賴喇嘛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Torghut Khan Ayuki's nephew Alabuzhur had sought passage through Dzungar lands to visit the Dalai Lama in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ayuki Khan of the Torghuts had a nephew Alabuzhur who asked passage through the Dzungars to Tibet to visit the Dalai Lama.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾台吉策妄阿喇布坦與阿玉奇構怨，阿喇布珠爾不得歸，款關乞內屬，詔封貝子，賜牧嘉峪關外黨色爾騰。

translations.literal: Dzungar taiji Tsewang Araptan feuded with Ayuki; Alabuzhur could not return, submitted at the frontier, was enfeoffed beile, and pastured outside Jiayuguan at Dangse'erteng.
translations.idiomatic: The Dzungar taiji Tsewang Araptan was at odds with Ayuki; Alabuzhur could not return, came to the border to seek incorporation, was enfeoffed as a beile, and was granted pasture outside Jiayuguan at Dangse'erteng.

sentences.zh: 嗣阿玉奇遣使入貢，上欲歸阿喇布珠爾。

translations.literal: When Ayuki later sent tribute, the emperor wished to send Alabuzhur back.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ayuki sent tribute envoys; the emperor wished to return Alabuzhur.

sentences.zh: 命圖理琛偕侍讀學士殷扎納、郎中納顏齎敕諭阿玉奇，假道鄂羅斯。

translations.literal: Tulichen was sent with Reader-Academician Yin Zhana and Director Nayin, bearing an edict to Ayuki via Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen was ordered, together with Reader-Academician Yin Zhana and Director Nayin, to carry an edict to Ayuki by way of Russia.

sentences.zh: 五月，圖理琛等自京師啟行，七月，至鄂羅斯境楚庫柏興。

translations.literal: They left the capital in the fifth month and reached Russian Chukoboin in the seventh.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tulichen and the others set out from the capital; in the seventh month they reached Chukoboin on Russian territory.

sentences.zh: 以假道故，待其國察罕汗進止。

translations.literal: As they traveled by leave of Russia, they waited on the tsar's permission.
translations.idiomatic: Because they were borrowing the route, they awaited the Russian tsar's decision.

sentences.zh: 五十二年正月，許假道，乃行。

translations.literal: In the first month of Kangxi 52 passage was granted and they departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifty-second year passage was granted and they set out.

sentences.zh: 還烏的柏興，越柏海爾湖而北，抵厄爾庫。

translations.literal: They went back to Udoboin, crossed Lake Baikal to the north, and reached Erku.
translations.idiomatic: They returned to Udoboin, crossed Lake Baikal northward, and reached Erku.

sentences.zh: 鄂羅斯託波爾噶噶林遣其屬博爾科尼來迎。

translations.literal: Tobolsk's governor-general sent Bolikoni to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The Russian Tobolsk governor-general sent his subordinate Bolikoni to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 噶噶林者，彼國所稱總管也。

translations.literal: Gagalin was their title for a regional governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gagalin was what that country called its chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛等欲行，博爾科尼言噶噶林令天使當自水路行，而昂噶拉河冰未泮，請稍駐俟之。

translations.literal: Bolikoni said the gagalin required travel by water, but the Angara was still frozen and asked them to wait.
translations.idiomatic: When Tulichen and the others wished to proceed, Bolikoni said the gagalin ordered the envoys to travel by water, but the Angara was not yet thawed and asked them to wait.

sentences.zh: 三月，自昂噶拉河乘舟抵伊聶謝柏興，登陸。

translations.literal: In the third month they boated up the Angara to Iakutsk and landed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they took boats on the Angara to Iakutsk and went ashore.

sentences.zh: 五月，抵麻科斯科，复乘舟自揭的河順流行，經那裡穆柏興、蘇爾呼特柏興、薩瑪爾斯科、狄穆演斯科諸地。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they reached Makovsk and again descended the Ket past Narym, Surgut, Samara, and Demyansk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they reached Makovsk; again they took boats down the Ket River, passing Narym, Surgut, Samara, and Demyansk.

sentences.zh: 七月，至託波爾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month they arrived at Tobolsk.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they reached Tobolsk.

sentences.zh: 其地噶噶林名馬提飛費多里魚赤，迎至廨，留八日。

translations.literal: Governor Matifeidoliyuchi received them at his yamen and kept them eight days.
translations.idiomatic: The local gagalin, Matifeidoliyuchi, welcomed them to his office and detained them eight days.

sentences.zh: 仍遣博爾科尼護之行，抵鴉班沁登陸。

translations.literal: Bolikoni escorted them again until they landed at Yabanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Bolikoni was again sent to escort them; they landed at Yabanchi.

sentences.zh: 自費耶爾和土爾斯科越佛落克嶺，抵索里喀穆斯科，以路濘，守凍十日。

translations.literal: From Feierhe Tversk they crossed Volok Pass to Solikamsk; mud forced a ten-day halt for frost.
translations.idiomatic: From Feierhe Tversk they crossed the Volok Ridge to Solikamsk; the road was mire and they waited on the freeze ten days.

sentences.zh: 復行，經改郭羅多、黑林諾付、喀山、西穆必爾斯科諸地。

translations.literal: They continued through Gaigoluo, Heilinofu, Kazan, and Simbirsk.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled on through Gaigoluo, Heilinofu, Kazan, and Simbirsk.

sentences.zh: 十一月，至薩拉託付，是為鄂羅斯與土爾扈特界。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they reached Saratov, the Russo-Torghut frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they reached Saratov, the border between Russia and the Torghuts.

sentences.zh: 水自東北來，折而南，鄂羅斯號為佛爾格，土爾扈特號為額濟勒。

translations.literal: A river ran from the northeast and turned south—the Russians called it the Volga, the Torghuts the Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Water came from the northeast and bent south; Russians called it the Volga, the Torghuts the Ili.

sentences.zh: 阿玉奇汗駐牧地曰瑪努託海，距此十日程，以雪盛不能行。

translations.literal: Ayuki pastured at Manutohai ten days distant, but deep snow blocked the way.
translations.idiomatic: Ayuki Khan's pasture was called Manutohai, ten days' journey away; heavy snow prevented travel.

sentences.zh: 五十三年四月，阿玉奇遣台吉祥偉徵等來迎。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Kangxi 53 Ayuki sent taiji Weizheng and others to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifty-third year Ayuki sent the taiji Weizheng and others to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 五月，圖理琛等渡額濟勒河，阿喇布珠爾之父納扎爾瑪穆特遣獻馬，卻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they crossed the Ili; Nazarmamut, Alabuzhur's father, offered horses, which they refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tulichen and the others crossed the Ili; Alabuzhur's father Nazarmamut sent horses as gifts, which they declined.

sentences.zh: 六年朔，至瑪努託海，阿玉奇擇日聽宣敕。

translations.literal: On the New Year of Kangxi 54 they reached Manutohai and Ayuki set a day to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's day of the fifty-fourth year they reached Manutohai; Ayuki chose a day to hear the edict proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛等以上意諭之曰：「阿喇布珠爾已賜爵優養，欲遣歸爾牧地，以策妄阿喇布坦方與爾交惡，恐為所戕。

translations.literal: They announced: 'Alabuzhur enjoys rank and stipend; we wish to restore him to your pastures, yet Tsewang Araptan is hostile and may harm him.'
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen and the others conveyed the imperial intent: 'Alabuzhur has been granted rank and generous maintenance. We wish to send him back to your pastures, but as Tsewang Araptan is now at enmity with you, we fear he may be killed.'

sentences.zh: 爾若欲令阿喇布珠爾歸，當自鄂羅斯來迎。

translations.literal: If you want him back, you must fetch him by way of Russia.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish Alabuzhur to return, you must come to meet him through Russia yourself.

sentences.zh: 」阿玉奇曰：「我雖外夷，然冠服與中國同。

translations.literal: ' Ayuki replied: 'I may be a foreigner, yet my dress matches China's.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ayuki said: 'Though I am an outer barbarian, my dress is the same as China's.

sentences.zh: 鄂羅斯乃嗜慾不同、言語不通之國也，天使歸道當察其情狀。

translations.literal: Russia is a land of alien customs and speech—the envoys should see it for themselves on the return journey.
translations.idiomatic: Russia is a land of different appetites and unintelligible speech; on your return you should observe its condition.

sentences.zh: 鄂羅斯若以往來數故不假道，則我無由入貢矣。

translations.literal: If Russia denies passage because of heavy traffic, I cannot reach you with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: If Russia, because of frequent traffic, refuses passage, I shall have no way to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 阿喇布珠爾荷厚恩，與歸土爾扈特同，復何疑慮？

translations.literal: Alabuzhur owes great favor; restoring him to the Torghuts is only just—why hesitate?
translations.idiomatic: Alabuzhur owes deep grace; his return to the Torghuts is the same—what doubt remains?

sentences.zh: 」阿玉奇及納扎爾瑪穆特等各贈馬及方物，圖理琛等以越境無私交，卻不受。

translations.literal: ' Ayuki and Nazarmamut offered horses and gifts, but the envoys refused private presents abroad.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ayuki and Nazarmamut each presented horses and local products; Tulichen and the others, having no private dealings across the border, declined them.

sentences.zh: 阿玉奇待之有隆禮，留十四日，筵宴不絕。

translations.literal: Ayuki entertained them lavishly for fourteen days without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Ayuki received them with great ceremony, keeping them fourteen days with feasting unceasing.

sentences.zh: 复附表奏謝。

translations.literal: He added a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛等遂行，由舊路歸，鄂羅斯遣護如初。

translations.literal: They left by the same road, again escorted by Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen and the others then departed, returned by the former route, and Russia sent escorts as before.

sentences.zh: 五十四年三月，還京師。

translations.literal: In the third month of Kangxi 54 they were back in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifty-fourth year they returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是役也，往返三載餘，經行數万裡。

translations.literal: The journey lasted over three years and crossed tens of thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: This mission lasted more than three years round trip and covered tens of thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 蓋土爾扈特為鄂羅斯所隔，遠阻聲教，而鄂羅斯又故導我使紆道行。

translations.literal: Russia separated the Torghuts from the court and deliberately sent the envoys by detours.
translations.idiomatic: The Torghuts were cut off by Russia, far from imperial influence, and Russia deliberately led our envoys by circuitous routes.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛奉使無辱命，既歸國，入對，述往還事狀，並撰異域錄，首冠輿圖，次為行記，呈上覽。

translations.literal: Tulichen discharged his mission honorably, reported to the throne, and wrote the Record of Foreign Lands with maps and a travelogue.
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen fulfilled his commission without disgrace; on returning he was received in audience, reported the journey, and compiled the Record of Foreign Lands, with maps first and a travel narrative following, which he presented for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 上嘉悅，尋授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and soon made him a vice director of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and soon appointed him vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 阿喇布珠爾亦遂留牧黨色爾騰不復遣，再傳至其子丹忠，雍正中，遷牧額濟內河。

translations.literal: Alabuzhur stayed at Dangse'erteng; his son Danzhong later moved the clan to the Ili in the Yongzheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Alabuzhur likewise remained pasturing at Dangse'erteng and was not sent back; the line passed to his son Danzhong, who in the Yongzheng reign moved pasture to the Ili.

sentences.zh: 圖理琛遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: Tulichen was transferred to director.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，命赴廣東察籓庫，就擢廣東布政使。

translations.literal: The Shizong sent him to inspect Guangdong's tribute silver and appointed him provincial treasurer there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong took the throne he was sent to Guangdong to inspect the tribute treasury and was promoted on the spot to provincial treasurer of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 調陝西。

translations.literal: He was moved to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3 he became governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to governor.

sentences.zh: 五年，召為兵部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was called to the Ministry of War as vice minister, then shifted to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned as vice minister of War and transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 偕喀爾喀郡王額駙策淩等往定喀爾喀與鄂羅斯界。

translations.literal: With Prince Consort Celeng of Khalkha he delimited the Khalkha-Russian border.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Khalkha prince consort Celeng and others he went to fix the border between Khalkha and Russia.

sentences.zh: 仍調兵部。

translations.literal: He returned to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to War.

sentences.zh: 六年，追議前定界時，與鄂羅斯使臣薩瓦鳴砲謝天，私立木牌，並擅納鄂羅斯貿易人入界；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was charged for firing salutes with the Russian envoy Sava, erecting private markers, and admitting Russian traders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on review of the earlier border mission, it was found that with the Russian envoy Sava he had fired cannon to thank Heaven, privately erected wooden markers, and on his own authority admitted Russian traders within the border;

sentences.zh: 又前任陝西巡撫時，將天下兵數繕摺私給將軍延信，逮問論斬。

translations.literal: As Shaanxi governor he had also secretly given General Yanxin a tally of national troop strength and was condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: and while previously governor of Shaanxi he had copied the empire's troop totals into a memorial and privately given it to General Yanxin; he was arrested and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 詔宥免，遣築扎克拜達里克城。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and sent to build Zhakebaidarike.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him and sent him to build the city of Zhakebaidarike.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，授內閣學士，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: The Gaozong made him a Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozong took the throne he was appointed Grand Secretariat academician and transferred to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以老解侍郎任，仍為內閣學士。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 1 he retired from the vice ministry on grounds of age but kept his academician title.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, on account of age he was released from the vice ministership but remained an academician.

sentences.zh: 二年，引疾去。

translations.literal: In the second year he resigned for illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he resigned citing illness.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died.

sentences.zh: 何國宗，字翰如，順天大興人。

translations.literal: He Guozong, courtesy name Hanru, was from Daxing in Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Guozong, style Hanru, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十一年進士，改庶吉士，命直內廷學算法。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of Kangxi 51, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and studied mathematics at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was ordered to study mathematics in the inner court.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，命編輯律曆淵源。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 52 he helped edit the Origins of Calendrical Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was ordered to edit the Origins of Calendrical Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 未散館，授編修。

translations.literal: Before leaving the Academy he was made a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving the Academy he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 三遷至庶子。

translations.literal: He rose through three steps to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，授侍讀學士，再遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng he became Reader-Academician, then Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was appointed Reader-Academician and was promoted again to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，命視黃、運河道，奏請增築戴村石壩，疏濬東昌城南七里河、城北魏家灣及德州城南減河；

translations.literal: In Yongzheng 3 he inspected the Yellow River and Grand Canal and proposed strengthening the Daicun stone dam and dredging rivers at Dongchang, Weijiawan, and Dezhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to inspect the Yellow River and Grand Canal waterways and memorialized to build up the stone dam at Daicun and dredge the Qili River south of Dongchang, Weijiawan north of the city, and the Jianhe south of Dezhou;

sentences.zh: 又以汶、泗泉源紆遠，請專設管泉通判；

translations.literal: he also urged a dedicated subprefect for the distant Wen and Si headwaters;
translations.idiomatic: and because the sources of the Wen and Si were far apart, he asked that a special subprefect manage the springs;

sentences.zh: 又請修高家堰石堤。

translations.literal: and repairs to the Gaojiayan stone dike.
translations.idiomatic: and he also asked to repair the stone embankment at Gaojiayan.

sentences.zh: 上皆允其請，並以高家堰石堤工衝要，命發帑興修。

translations.literal: The throne approved all requests and funded the critical Gaojiayan works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all his requests, and because the Gaojiayan works were critical, ordered funds disbursed for construction.

sentences.zh: 復奏言：「運河自臨清以上，賴衛水以濟。

translations.literal: He added: 'North of Linqing the canal depends on the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: 'Above Linqing the canal relies on the Wei River to supply it.

sentences.zh: 衛水發源百泉，益以丹、洹二水，其流始盛。

translations.literal: The Wei begins at the Hundred Springs and grows only after the Dan and Huan join it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei rises at the Hundred Springs, augmented by the Dan and Huan, and only then becomes ample.

sentences.zh: 請疏百泉為三渠，洹河亦筑壩開渠引水，一分灌田，三分濟運。

translations.literal: He proposed splitting the Hundred Springs into three channels and damming the Huan so one share irrigated fields and three fed transport.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to divide the Hundred Springs into three channels and to build dams and canals on the Huan, one part for irrigation and three parts for transport.

sentences.zh: 」上從其議。

translations.literal: ' The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 旋以山東巡撫塞楞額奏言國宗等奉使所經州縣，供億白金七千六百有奇。

translations.literal: Soon Shandong Governor Saileng'e reported counties along Guozong's route had spent over 7,600 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Shandong governor Saileng'e memorialized that the counties Guozong's mission passed through had supplied more than seven thousand six hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 上責國宗不惜物力，負任使，坐降調。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Guozong for waste, faulted his mission conduct, and demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Guozong for not sparing resources, held him responsible for the mission, and demoted him.

sentences.zh: 五年，授大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he became president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 六年，复擢內閣學士，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again made academician and vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was again promoted to Grand Secretariat academician and transferred to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，命與侍郎牛鈕督修北運河減水壩，並濬引河。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he and Vice Minister Niu Niu supervised Northern Canal flood dams and dredging.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was ordered, together with Vice Minister Niu Niu, to supervise repair of flood-relief dams on the Northern Canal and dredging of diversion channels.

sentences.zh: 國宗等議捍護河西務北堤及耍兒渡魚鱗壩，別開塌河淀下流賈家沽洩水河，建築三里淺、筐兒港、張家莊諸處挑水壩，上命如議速行。

translations.literal: They proposed bank works at Hexiwu, the Shua'erdu fish-scale dam, a Jiajiagu drain, and diversion dams at Sanliqian, Kuang'ergang, and Zhangjiazhuang—the emperor ordered rapid action.
translations.idiomatic: Guozong and others proposed protecting the north bank at Hexiwu and the Yulin dam at Shua'erdu, opening a drainage channel at Jiajiagu below the Tahe marshes, and building diversion dams at Sanliqian, Kuang'ergang, and Zhangjiazhuang; the emperor ordered these carried out swiftly.

sentences.zh: 九年，兼河東河道總督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he also became director-general of Hedong waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he concurrently served as director-general of the Hedong waterways.

sentences.zh: 田文鏡奏戴村初建玲瓏、亂石、滾水三壩。

translations.literal: Tian Wenjing memorialized that at Daicun the Linglong, Luan-shi, and Gun-shui dams had first been built.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wenjing reported that Daicun originally had Linglong, rubble, and rolling-water dams.

sentences.zh: 汶水盛漲，自壩面流入鹽河歸海。

translations.literal: When the Wen River swelled, water flowed over the dam face into the salt river and out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wen flooded, water spilled over the dam into the salt river and to the sea.

sentences.zh: 國宗等增築石壩，水不能過，瀕河連年被患。

translations.literal: Guozong and others raised the stone dam higher so water could not pass; districts along the river suffered flood year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Guozong's raised stone dam blocked the flow and brought floods year after year along the river.

sentences.zh: 請毀石壩，復為亂石、滾水壩。

translations.literal: They asked to destroy the stone dam and restore the rubble and rolling-water dams.
translations.idiomatic: They urged tearing down the stone dam and restoring the rubble and rolling-water structures.

sentences.zh: 上責國宗勘工錯誤，貽害民間，奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Guozong for surveying errors that harmed the people and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Guozong for faulty engineering that hurt the populace and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，起充算學館、律呂館總裁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianlong he was recalled to serve as chief compiler of the Mathematics Institute and the Pitch-Pipe Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong he was reappointed chief compiler of the Mathematics and Pitch-Pipe institutes.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜秩視三品。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was granted rank equivalent to third grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received third-grade rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授左副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十年，兼領飲天監正。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he concurrently served as director of the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he also headed the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，聖祖命製皇輿全覽圖，以天度定準望，一度當二百里，遣使如奉天，循行混同、鴨綠二江，至朝鮮分界處，測繪為圖。

translations.literal: During Kangxi the Shengzu ordered the compilation of the Complete Imperial Atlas, fixing bearings by celestial degrees with one degree equal to two hundred li, and sent envoys to Fengtian to follow the Hun and Yalu rivers to the Korean border and survey maps.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi the Shengzu commissioned the Complete Imperial Atlas, using celestial measurement at two hundred li per degree, and sent surveyors from Fengtian along the Hun and Yalu to Korea's border.

sentences.zh: 以鴨綠、圖門二江間未詳晰，五十年，命烏喇總管穆克登偕按事部員復往詳察。

translations.literal: Because the stretch between the Yalu and Tumen was not clear, in the fiftieth year Mukedeng, commander at Ula, was ordered with ministry officials on mission to investigate again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Yalu-Tumen sector remained unclear, so in Kangxi 50 Mukedeng of Ula and ministry agents were sent to survey it again.

sentences.zh: 國宗弟國棟亦以通曆法直內廷。

translations.literal: Guozong's younger brother Guodong also, for mastery of calendrical methods, served in the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Guodong, skilled in calendrical science, also served at court.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，命國棟等周歷江以南諸行省，測北極高度及日景。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year Guodong and others were ordered to tour the provinces south of the Yangzi and measure polar altitude and solar shadow.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 53 Guodong was sent through the southern provinces to measure polar altitude and noon shadows.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，圖成，為全圖一，離合凡三十二幀，別為分省圖，省各一幀。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year the atlas was finished: one complete map in thirty-two folding sheets, with separate provincial sheets, one per province.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 58 the atlas was complete—thirty-two folios for the whole empire plus one sheet per province.

sentences.zh: 命蔣廷錫示群臣，諭曰：「朕費三十餘年心力，始得告成。

translations.literal: Jiang Tingxi was ordered to show it to the ministers, with the instruction: 'I spent more than thirty years of effort before this could be completed.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Jiang Tingxi present it to the ministers, saying: 'More than thirty years of my labor went into this work.'

sentences.zh: 山脈水道，俱與禹貢合。

translations.literal: Mountain ranges and waterways all accord with the Yu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Its mountains and rivers match the Yu Gong.

sentences.zh: 爾以此與九卿詳閱，如有不合處，九卿有知者，舉出奏明。

translations.literal: Take this and have the Nine Ministers examine it in detail; if anything is incorrect and any minister knows it, let him report it.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Nine Ministers study it; whoever finds an error should report it.

sentences.zh: 」乃鐫以銅版，藏內府。

translations.literal: ' It was then engraved on copper plates and stored in the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: ' The plates were cast in copper and stored in the imperial vault.

sentences.zh: 高宗既定準噶爾，乾隆二十一年，命國宗偕侍衛努克三、哈清阿率欽天監西洋人往伊犁，自巴里坤分西北兩路，測天度繪圖。

translations.literal: After the Gaozong had pacified the Dzungars, in the twenty-first year of Qianlong he ordered Guozong, together with the guardsmen Nukesan and Haking'a, to lead Westerners of the Astronomical Bureau to Ili; from Barkul they divided into northwest routes to measure celestial degrees and draw maps.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the Dzungars, in Qianlong 21 Guozong, Nukesan, Haking'a, and Astronomical Bureau Jesuits surveyed Ili from Barkul in northwestern teams.

sentences.zh: 既還報，命署左都御史。

translations.literal: On their return and report he was ordered to act as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After they reported back he was appointed acting Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 以京察舉弟國棟，​​坐徇庇，奪官。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation he recommended his brother Guodong; for favoritism he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended his brother Guodong at the capital review and lost his post for favoritism.

sentences.zh: 尋授編修，直上書房。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed compiler and served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a compiler in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，复授內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again appointed Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he again became a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 是歲，上以諸回部悉定，復遣尚書明安圖等往測天度繪圖，是為乾隆內府皇輿圖。

translations.literal: That year, because all the Muslim regions were now settled, the emperor again sent Minister Ming Antu and others to measure celestial degrees and draw maps—this was the Qianlong inner-court imperial atlas.
translations.idiomatic: That year, with the Muslim regions pacified, Ming Antu and others surveyed anew for the Qianlong palace atlas.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，以老休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he retired for old age.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-first year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國家撫有疆宇，謂之版圖，版言乎其有民，圖言乎其有地。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the state pacifies its territory it is called ban tu—ban speaks of having people, tu of having land.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary observes: A pacified realm is called ban tu—ban denotes its people, tu its terrain.

sentences.zh: 聖祖東訪長白山，西探河源，北撫土爾扈特，武默訥、舒蘭、圖理琛奉使稱職。

translations.literal: The Shengzu visited Changbai in the east, explored the river source in the west, and soothed the Torghuts in the north; Wumune, Shulan, and Tulichen discharged their missions faithfully.
translations.idiomatic: The Shengzu worshipped at Changbai, traced the Yellow River's source, and received the Torghuts; Wumune, Shulan, and Tulichen served with distinction.

sentences.zh: 觀所還奏，曲折詳盡，歷歷如繪。

translations.literal: Judging from their returned memorials, the accounts are winding yet thorough, vivid as painting.
translations.idiomatic: Their memorials are intricate yet complete, vivid as painted scrolls.

sentences.zh: 國宗以明算事聖祖，又幸老壽，迨高宗朝，詣新疆測繪。

translations.literal: Guozong, skilled in calculation, served the Shengzu; blessed with long life, he went in the Gaozong reign to survey Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guozong's mathematics served Kangxi; he lived long enough to survey Xinjiang under Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 康熙、乾隆兩內府圖皆躬與編摹。

translations.literal: He personally took part in editing both the Kangxi and Qianlong palace atlases.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile both the Kangxi and Qianlong palace maps.

sentences.zh: 揆之於古，其裴秀、賈耽之倫歟？

translations.literal: Measured against antiquity, is he not of the company of Pei Xiu and Jia Dan?
translations.idiomatic: By ancient standards, does he not rank with Pei Xiu and Jia Dan?
